messages:
support-jen: Hey team, escalated P0 from PolymerHealth — after users complete SSO + MFA they get bounced back to login immediately. Customer says it started after our auth-service deploy on 2026-03-10. Repro steps from them:
1) Go to https://app.polymerhealth.com
2) Click Sign in -> redirects to okta.polymerhealth.com -> MFA flow -> redirect back to https://app.polymerhealth.com/auth/callback
3) Instead of being logged in they see the login page again.
They attached a trace id `trace_5f2b9c` and request id `req-abc123`. Happens mostly on Safari iOS and some Chrome incognito windows. Can we triage? :eyes:

alex: thanks Jen — can you paste the exact Set-Cookie headers they captured and confirm whether the SSO redirect crosses domains (it does) and whether the cookie Domain is set to a parent domain? Also, do they use any iframe flows?

support-jen: pasted what the customer captured (redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: https://app.polymerhealth.com/auth/callback?code=XXX&state=YYY
Set-Cookie: session=eyJ...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure
Set-Cookie: id_token=eyJ...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; Max-Age=3600
```
Note: there is no Domain nor SameSite on the session cookie. They also gave a curl capture showing that after following redirects the Cookie header is not sent to the app on the final request.

idp-team: we pulled the logs for req-abc123 — the auth-service issued the session cookie after the OIDC callback. The code path that writes cookies is in auth/handlers/sessions.go. Recent change in that PR (deploy 2026-03-10) added a cookie rotation step but I see we didn't explicitly set SameSite or Domain. Logs:```
[2026-03-10T14:02:12Z] INFO auth: completed callback set-cookie session=*** req=req-abc123 trace=trace_5f2b9c
```

eng-sre-chris: probable root cause: cross-site redirect + cookie defaults. Browsers will treat cookies without SameSite as Lax (or stricter), and Safari iOS has ITP/third-party restrictions that can block cookies on cross-site POST/redirect flows, especially for auth flows that land via a redirect. Because the auth redirect goes from okta.polymerhealth.com -> auth.redwood-inference.com -> app.polymerhealth.com, cookies written on auth.redwood-inference.com that lack Domain=.polymerhealth.com will not be sent to app.polymerhealth.com. Also missing SameSite=None prevents cookies from being sent on cross-site navigations in some clients.

security-lucy: adding to that — we should also confirm refresh token TTL and whether cookie Max-Age aligns with token expiry. Mismatch could make the frontend think session expired. But the absent Domain/SameSite is suspicious for Safari case.

support-jen: customer also noted the redirect chain sometimes includes our CDN host `edge.cloudflare.com` which may rewrite headers. They captured a full chain showing Set-Cookie at `auth.redwood-inference.com` then subsequent redirect to `app.polymerhealth.com` where browser doesn't send the cookie.

alex: can someone paste the current cookie code snippet? Need to check flags we set.

eng-sre-chris: here is the relevant snippet from sessions.go (current prod):
```
http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
  Name:  "session",
  Value: token,
  Path:  "/",
  HttpOnly: true,
  Secure: true,
  // no Domain, no SameSite configured
})
```
We should update to explicitly set Domain and SameSite=None for cross-site SSO flows, e.g.:
```
Domain: ".polymerhealth.com",
SameSite: http.SameSiteNoneMode,
```
But we need to be careful: for multi-tenant customers the domain must be dynamic. If customers use their own custom domain we need to compute it from the SP metadata or fallback to using the auth cookie only on the auth domain and rely on top-level redirect.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: auth-service v2026.03.10 (sha: b7cfa2) — triggered by PR #1124 — owner: eng-auth

eng-sre-chris: proposed mitigation (short term):
- Set SameSite=None and Secure explicitly when issuing session cookies for OIDC flows.
- If a customer uses a custom domain (app.*), set Domain to their apex (computed from request Host) when trusted.
- Add a fallback: after callback, if cookie not present on subsequent request, call a server-side cookie-regenerate endpoint that issues a cookie with Domain/SameSite set for the app domain.
- Add a smoke test that exercises SSO flow in Safari iOS simulator.
This is a P0 for support — I'll open a hotfix branch.

idp-team: quick questions — for customers on our Hosted flow (where we host auth.redwood-inference.com) we may not be able to set Domain to .customer.com. For those we should keep cookie on our domain and ensure the final redirect to the app includes a signed token in the URL fragment that the app can exchange. That is more secure and avoids cross-domain cookie problems.

eng-sre-chris: agreed. Two parallel tracks: 1) quick patch to make SameSite explicit so Safari/Lax issues are reduced; 2) product change to support token-exchange on final app domain for hosted tenants.

security-lucy: also please add a short review for CSRF implications when switching SameSite to None. Ensure double-submit or state param is enforced for callback flows.

support-jen: I ran a quick repro locally with curl to emulate redirects and observed cookie drop. Curl snippet:```
curl -i -L -c cookies.txt 'https://auth.redwood-inference.com/oidc/callback?code=XXX'
# cookies.txt shows session cookie set but subsequent GET to https://app.polymerhealth.com does not include session in header
```
I'll attach the trace and customer capture to the ticket.

eng-sre-chris: action items:
- chris (eng-sre) will open hotfix branch and PR to set SameSite=None and explicit Domain when tenant domain is known (ETA 2h).
- idp-team to validate behaviour for hosted tenants and propose token-exchange fallback (ETA EOD).
- security-lucy to review CSRF and refresh token TTL (ETA 4h).
- support-jen to inform customer about temporary workaround: suggest using non-incognito Chrome or desktop until we patch; ask them to confirm whether they use custom domains or CNAMEs.

support-jen: assigned and noted in ticket — I updated the customer: they saw :thumbsup: and will test again after patch.

eng-sre-chris: PR opened: https://git.redwood-inference.com/auth-service/pulls/1177 — includes tests and a flag to enable SameSite=None by env (AUTH_COOKIE_SAMESITE=None). Will run staging canary and then promote.

sre-bot: Canary deploy started for auth-service v2026.03.10-hotfix (canary=10%) — monitor: http://grafana.internal/d/uuid/auth-service-sso?orgId=1

support-jen: update for customer — small number of users still hitting issue in Safari after canary, but majority fixed. Will keep opened until 48h of no reports. Thanks all. :lock:
